label: Person
name: Thomas Aquinas
summary:
Thomas Aquinas (1225–1274) was an Italian Dominican friar, philosopher, and theologian who synthesized Aristotelian philosophy with Christian theology — a monumental intellectual achievement that remains the foundation of Catholic thought. His 'Summa Theologica' is one of the most influential works in Western philosophy.

Born to Italian nobility near Naples, he chose the life of a mendicant friar against his family's wishes. At the University of Paris and in Rome, he produced an astonishing body of work: the 'Summa Theologica,' 'Summa contra Gentiles,' and commentaries on Aristotle that demonstrated faith and reason were complementary, not contradictory.

His 'Five Ways' — five arguments for God's existence from natural reason — became the cornerstone of natural theology. Pope Leo XIII declared Thomism the official philosophy of the Catholic Church in 1879. Aquinas remains the most important philosopher-theologian in Christian history.
